reasons: Claimed status is compliant, and consistent with that no redline or comment was proposed — the rendered paragraphs are identical to the originals, so there is no invalid or directionally wrong edit to correct.

The cited text supports compliance: Section 3.1 (p0248) grants exclusivity in favour of Sanofi (our party), which the rule expressly treats as acceptable; Article VII (p0358–p0360) contains no requirements, sole-source or 'purchase all requirements' commitment — Section 7.2 in fact obliges RevMed to help Sanofi stand up its own third-party supply, and Section 7.3 only requires good-faith negotiation where a Party actually manufactures for the other.

The rationale properly notes rather than flags Section 12.2(d) (p0493): it is a conditional termination right triggered only if Sanofi pursues a Competing Product without having commenced a Registrational Clinical Trial, not an affirmative exclusive-dealing covenant restricting sourcing; treating it as a noted sub-element rather than a deviation matches the playbook's classification semantics.

Deterministic check ('no requirements/sole-supplier obligation on Customer remains') passes, corroborating the compliant classification; the finding is retained as internal evidence and correctly raises no negotiation issue.
